jobs.title: Network Developer
jobs.description: Senior Network Developer About Share Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served. The Role Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices. You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team. What you'll do Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time. Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist. Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable. Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change. Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop. Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system. Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off. Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you. Our Ideal Candidate 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP. Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit. Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense. Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you. You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe. You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed. AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't. You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network. A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders. Nice to have Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale. Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them

jobs.title: Network Operation Engineer
jobs.description: Network Operations Engineer 1. About the role Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it. For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar. We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling. The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes. You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it. 2. What you'll do Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing. Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with. Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state. Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online. Move the work forward. You are part of the network team

jobs.title: (Junior) Creative Director – Design & Brand (m/w/d)
jobs.description: Deine Rolle Die Beratungsbranche in Deutschland sieht überall gleich aus. Gleiche Bildwelten, gleiche Stockfotos, gleiche Blautöne, gleiche Sprache. Marke ist in diesem Markt praktisch unbesetzt. Vogel ist eine der erfolgreichsten mittelständischen Beratungsgesellschaften in Deutschland — mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen vertrauen uns ihre Steuer-, kaufmännischen und strategischen Themen an. Etablierte Mandanten, lange Erfahrung, starke Wachstumsbasis. Daraus bauen wir das Beratungshaus für den deutschen Mittelstand, und wir bauen es schnell. Diesen Markt gewinnt nicht, wer den besseren Fachaufsatz schreibt, sondern wer als Marke dauerhaft präsent ist und den Markt anführt — bei Unternehmern genauso wie bei den Menschen, die wir für uns gewinnen wollen. Genau diese Marke bauen wir: ikonisch, unverwechselbar, und in dieser Branche gibt es sie noch nicht. Design ist deshalb keine Abteilung am Ende der Kette: Was wir bauen, wird aus einer Designperspektive gedacht. Du bist Grafikdesigner mit außergewöhnlichem visuellem Gespür und einem Portfolio, das für sich spricht. Du kommst aus einer Agentur, einem eigenen Studio oder von einer Marke mit starkem visuellem System. Du wechselst, weil du dort immer nur einen Teilbereich verantwortest — eine Kampagne, ein Relaunch, eine Strecke im System — und nie die Marke als Ganzes samt der Experience dahinter verantworten und führen darfst. Genau das willst du: die volle visuelle Verantwortung, mit einem Auftraggeber, der dir das Urteil nicht wegnimmt. Die Rolle ist bewusst nach unten offen. Wenn du gerade aus einem starken Gestaltungsstudium oder einer gestalterischen Ausbildung kommst und deine Mappe das visuelle Urteil und die Systemtiefe zeigt, die diese Rolle braucht, bist du hier richtig — du startest dann am unteren Ende der Spanne, arbeitest zunächst an Teilen des Systems und wächst in die volle Verantwortung hinein. Das Portfolio entscheidet, nicht das Jahr des Abschlusses. Bei Vogel findest du beides: Strukturen, die tragen, und ein Setup, das jeden Tag nach vorne geht. Kein Konzern-Korsett. Kein Aufbau-Versprechen ohne Boden. Du verantwortest das gesamte visuelle System von Vogel und der weiteren Marken, die daneben entstehen — Print, Digital, Raum, Bewegtbild, Experience. Du setzt selbst um und ziehst Partner dort zu, wo Kapazität oder Spezialisierung es erfordert. Du berichtest direkt an die Geschäftsführung. Die Rolle sitzt in München, vor Ort. Die natürliche Entwicklung führt nach 24 bis 36 Monaten in die fachliche Führung des Design- und Brand-Bereichs. Deine Verantwortung Visuelles System und Markenführung Du verantwortest das Designsystem von Vogel — Typografie, Farbe, Bildsprache, Layout-Prinzipien, Komponenten — und entwickelst es weiter, statt es nur zu verwalten. Du überträgst das System in Content: Social, Publikationen, Whitepaper, Präsentationen, Recruiting-Material. Das System ist erst fertig, wenn andere im Unternehmen damit arbeiten können, ohne dich zu fragen. Du setzt die visuellen Systeme der weiteren Marken auf, die bei Vogel entstehen. Dein Maßstab: Wer drei unserer Touchpoints nebeneinander sieht, erkennt sie ohne Logo als Vogel. Gestaltung über alle Medien Print: Publikationen, Geschäftsausstattung, Mandantenkommunikation, Kampagnenmotive — von der ersten Skizze bis zur Druckfreigabe in deiner Hand. Webdesign: Du gestaltest vogel-beratung.com und die dazugehörigen Seiten weiter, im direkten Austausch mit unserem Webentwickler. Darüber hinaus verantwortest du das Webdesign für alle Standorte und Gesellschaften der Vogel-Gruppe. Eventdesign und räumliche Gestaltung: Standorte, Bühnen, eigene Veranstaltungsformate, Messeauftritte. Du gestaltest, wie Vogel sich anfühlt, wenn man im Raum steht. Experience Design: Du denkst den Weg von Mandanten und Bewerbern als gestaltete Abfolge, nicht als Sammlung einzelner Assets. Kreativ-Steuerung, Partner und Nachwuchs Du steuerst Agenturen, Kreativpartner, Fotografen und Freelancer — Briefing, Auswahl, Qualität

Als Social Media Manager (m/w/d) unterstützt du uns dabei, unsere Social-Media-Kanäle weiterzuentwickeln – von der ersten Content-Idee über die Produktion bis zur Veröffentlichung. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unserem Content-, Brand- und Podcast-Team zusammen und bringst deine eigenen Ideen und dein Gespür für guten Social Content ein. Von Anfang an übernimmst du Verantwortung für eigene Themen und Formate. Ob Social Posts, Reels, Podcast-Clips oder Event-Content: Du hilfst uns dabei, komplexe Finanz- und Investmentthemen verständlich, relevant und visuell stark für Social Media aufzubereiten. Was machst du dabei konkret? Social Media & Planung: Du betreust unsere Kanäle auf Instagram, LinkedIn und Facebook und planst gemeinsam mit dem Team, welche Themen und Formate wann und wo stattfinden. Content Creation: Du entwickelst Posts, Carousels, Reels und Stories von der Idee bis zur Umsetzung. Gleichzeitig machst du aus bestehenden Inhalten wie Magazinartikeln, Marktkommentaren, Interviews, Events oder Expertengesprächen eigenständigen Social Content – von starken Hooks und Captions bis zu Recaps und Key Takeaways. Podcast & Video: Du unterstützt bei der Produktion von That’s Smart Money und entwickelst aus unseren Gesprächen relevante Clips und Short-Form-Content. Dabei arbeitest du unter anderem mit Riverside und unseren Video-Tools. Trends & neue Ideen: Du beobachtest, welche Formate und Mechaniken auf Social Media funktionieren, und überlegst, was davon zu LIQID passt. Gute Ideen sollst du bei uns nicht nur vorschlagen, sondern auch ausprobieren können. DAS BRINGST DU MIT Du verstehst Social Media und hast bereits selbst Content gemacht: Ob für einen eigenen Account, ein Projekt, dein Studium oder ein Unternehmen, ist für uns zweitrangig. Entscheidend ist, dass du ein gutes Gespür dafür hast, was auf Social Media funktioniert. Du kannst Geschichten erzählen und richtig gut schreiben: Du erkennst den interessanten Gedanken in einem Thema, findest einen starken Einstieg und kannst auch komplexere Inhalte verständlich und präzise auf den Punkt bringen. Du hast ein gutes visuelles Gespür und Lust auf Produktion: Fotografie, Typografie, Layout und Video interessieren dich und du setzt Content gerne selbst um. Erfahrung mit Riverside, CapCut, Premiere oder ähnlichen Tools ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss. Du packst selbst an: Du arbeitest eigenständig und zuverlässig, bringst Ideen mit und hast Lust, Verantwortung für eigene Themen und Formate zu übernehmen. Du bist neugierig auf Finanzthemen: Du musst noch kein Investment-Profi sein. Aber Wirtschaft, Märkte und Investments interessieren dich und du hast Lust, dich auch in komplexere Themen einzuarbeiten. Du arbeitest gerne im Team: Du hast Spaß daran, gemeinsam mit Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus Content, Brand, Podcast und anderen Bereichen aus einer guten Idee richtig guten Content zu machen. So geht es für dich weiter Eine ausgezeichnete Candidate Experience und Transparenz haben für uns im Interviewprozess höchste Priorität. Die verschiedenen Bewerbungsphasen helfen uns zu verstehen, wie eine Zusammenarbeit aussehen könnte – und geben dir gleichzeitig die Möglichkeit, LIQID und das Team kennenzulernen. Erstes virtuelles Kennenlernen mit unserer Social Media Managerin Verena: Wir tauschen uns darüber aus, ob deine Erfahrungen und Erwartungen an die Position mit unseren Anforderungen übereinstimmen. Kleine praktische Aufgabe: Du bekommst eine Aufgabe, die sich an typischen Themen aus deinem zukünftigen Arbeitsalltag orientiert. So sehen wir, wie du Content denkst und umsetzt – und du bekommst einen konkreten Eindruck von der Rolle. Gespräch mit unserer Hiring Managerin Lenika & Team: Wir tauchen

jobs.title: (Senior) Customer Success Manager (f/m/d)
jobs.description: UNSER PURPOSE BEI PLANCRAFT Gemeinsam das Rückgrat des europäischen Handwerks aufbauen – mit moderner Software und smarten AI-Lösungen. jobs.title: Senior Product Owner – Xsolla Money Account
jobs.description: ABOUT YOU   We are seeking an experienced Senior Product Owner to help define, build, and scale the Xsolla Money Account. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in complex problem spaces, enjoys working hands-on with engineering and partners, and is motivated by turning ambiguity into shipped, high-quality products. The Xsolla Money Account is a strategic initiative to build embedded financial services for gamers, creators, and developers. The product spans wallet capabilities, card issuing, payouts, and future financial tools that remove friction from how value moves across the gaming ecosystem. Sitting at the intersection of fintech and gaming, the Money Account enables new business models, creator monetization, and deeper player engagement. You will own critical parts of the Money Account roadmap and execution, working closely with cross-functional teams and external partners to deliver intuitive, reliable, and scalable financial products. Success in this role requires strong product judgment, technical fluency, the ability to navigate ambiguity in a dynamic environment with shifting priorities, and consistent follow-through from concept through launch and iteration. This role is best suited for someone who enjoys staying close to execution and takes pride in seeing complex work through to completion. This is a high-impact product area operating in a dynamic, evolving environment with meaningful technical, regulatory, and partner complexity. The opportunity is to shape foundational financial infrastructure that will scale globally and directly influence how money flows through the gaming economy.   ABOUT US   Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. With more paths to profits and ways to win, developers have all the things needed to enjoy the game.   For more information, visit  xsolla.com . Responsibilities: Product Strategy & Roadmap Contribute to the Money Account product strategy and roadmap in alignment with business objectives and customer needs. Identify opportunities to expand wallet, issuing, payouts, and related financial capabilities for gamers and creators. Balance user experience, technical feasibility, regulatory considerations, and partner constraints when shaping solutions. Product Definition & Delivery Translate product strategy into clear, high-quality PRDs that provide context, rationale, and actionable requirements. Partner closely with UX/UI designers to craft intuitive, trustworthy end-to-end user experiences. Work with engineering teams using Jira and Confluence to manage scope, priorities, and delivery. Drive features from ideation through build, testing, launch readiness, and post-launch iteration. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate closely with engineering, design, data, compliance, legal, finance, marketing, and customer support teams. Communicate goals, tradeoffs, and timelines clearly to maintain alignment across stakeholders. Support internal enablement by helping teams understand new features, user flows, and operational impacts. Partner & Platform Engagement Work with external partners such as wallet providers, issuing banks, BaaS platforms, and card networks. Participate in partner discussions to clarify requirements, dependencies, and delivery expectations. Contribute to evaluations of vendors, platforms, and capabilities that support the Money Acco

jobs.description: Deine Aufgaben Wir bauen die Software, mit der Mieterstromprojekte laufen: Zählerdaten rein, Abrechnung raus, und alles dazwischen. Der Weg dahin ist bewusst gewählt: Du startest für rund sechs Monate als Entwickler im Core Team. Du baust Features, machst Reviews und lernst Codebasis, Fachlichkeit und Menschen von innen kennen. Danach übernimmst du die Führung des Teams. Wer ein Team führen will, das er nie von innen gesehen hat, führt es an dem vorbei, was zählt. Technisch: Python mit Django und Django Ninja im Backend, React mit TypeScript im Frontend, PostgreSQL mit TimescaleDB, deployt auf Kubernetes per GitOps mit ArgoCD. KI-Coding-Assistenten sind fester Teil des Workflows. In den ersten Monaten schreibst du diesen Code selbst. Danach musst du ihn weiter lesen können und verstehen, worüber dein Team diskutiert. In den ersten sechs Monaten Du arbeitest als Entwickler im Core Team: Features end-to-end, Reviews, Deployments, Support-Fälle. Die Menschen im Team sind deine erste Verantwortung Du verantwortest die Lieferung: Zusammen mit Product priorisierst du nach wirtschaftlichem Wert und regulatorischem Druck, planst realistisch und sorgst dafür, dass Zugesagtes fertig wird Du bringst Fachverständnis in die Produktentscheidungen ein: Du erkennst, wann eine Anforderung aus dem Markt kommt, wann aus einem einzelnen Kunden, und wann aus einem Missverständnis Du hältst die technische Qualität hoch, ohne selbst der Flaschenhals zu sein: Du moderierst Architekturentscheidungen, forderst Tests und Reviews ein und schaffst Raum für Refactoring Du bist die Schnittstelle zu Product, Support und den anderen Engineering-Teams, und du löst Konflikte, bevor sie im Sprint landen Du machst Probleme sichtbar: Wenn etwas nicht klappt, sagst du es früh und mit Vorschlag statt spät und mit Ausrede Du gestaltest Prozesse so, dass sie dem Team dienen, und schaffst die ab, die es nicht tun Dein Profil Mehrere Jahre Erfahrung als Softwareentwickler mit Web-Anwendungen in Produktion. jobs.title: Senior Product Developer – Candy & Confectionery (All Genders)

We make the snacks everyone actually craves: chocolate bars, protein bars, wafers, cookies, gummies and more. Our products contain up to 90% less sugar with zero compromise on taste. We are a 130-person team based in Hamburg, with our own lab, a portfolio of more than 170 SKUs and ambitious growth plans across D2C, retail, Amazon and Europe. We are looking for a Senior Product Developer for Candy & Confectionery to own the technical development of our portfolio from the first brief through formulation, sensory validation, scale-up and launch. As our Senior Product Developer, you will bring technical depth to one of our most important categories and make sure every decision works in the real world: in the recipe, in the factory and in the customer’s hands. Are you a food developer who knows how to turn a great idea into a product people genuinely love? Someone who can balance taste, texture, stability, cost, compliance and timing while getting the product over the line? If you like taking ownership and enjoy solving real product problems, we would love to hear from you! YOUR TASKS End-to-End Product Development: You own candy and confectionery projects from brief to launch. You translate requirements into clear technical targets, develop and optimise formulations, oversee trials, sensory validation and technical decisions. Sugar Reduction & Product Performance: You develop reduced-sugar and no-added-sugar products without compromising on taste. You understand how ingredients affect texture, processing, stability and shelf life, and make clear trade-offs between quality, cost, compliance and speed. Sensory, Shelf Life & Scale-Up: You plan and coordinate sensory, shelf-life and stability testing. You prepare for pilot and industrial trials, work closely with co-manufacturers, troubleshoot issues and follow solutions through to production. Specifications, Suppliers & Compliance: You manage formulations, specifications, technical documentation, ingredients and samples. Together with our Quality team, you ensure that food law, labelling, allergen, nutritional and claims requirements are considered from the start. Cross-Functional Ownership: You work closely with Product, Quality, Operations, Procurement, Brand, Retail and Marketing. You communicate clearly, flag risks early, challenge assumptions and keep projects moving. Building Better NPD Processes: You document decisions and learnings, create clear handovers and help make product development more structured and predictable as ahead grows. YOUR PROFILE You bring 5+ years of experience in food product development, R&D, or NPD, with a track record from brief through formulation, sensory validation, scale-up, and launch. Hands-on experience in gummies, candy, chocolate, confectionery, or a related sweet-goods category is mandatory. You understand how taste, texture, processing, stability, shelf life, ingredients and production realities come together in a successful product. You have experience with sugar-reduction or no-added-sugar systems and know how to balance product performance with consumer expectations. You have worked with ingredient suppliers and co-manufacturers and have been involved in pilot or industrial-scale production. You are comfortable with specifications, technical documentation, and food-law requirements. You take ownership and follow through. You are structured without being bureaucratic, comfortable with ambiguity and willing to challenge a brief, assumption or timeline when needed. You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and enjoy working as a senior individual contributor without direct reports initially. You hold a degree or equivalent training in food science, food technology, chemistry, nutrition science, ecotrophology, or a comparable field. You communicate confidently in German and English. Depending on your client’s needs, you’ll take on a range of roles. These will include:   ·       Taking the lead on responding to outages, triaging issues, balancing stakeholder priorities/concerns, and keeping communication channels open with all parties. ·       Designing, developing, and implementing continuous deployment solutions that help our clients to deliver software faster and more efficiently. ·       Collaborating with our clients to understand their ways of working and will have an enthusiasm to learn new tools and technologies as needed. ·       Helping and mentoring other developers so that they can achieve their full potential ·       Contributing within Opencast communities. · Ensure that work is carried out in accordance with Opencast's quality, environmental, and information security policies and procedures, as well as applicable customer policies, standards, and procedures while working on client.    We care about building things right. People to support you every step of the way.    Where you’ll work    Your working time at Opencast will be split between multiple locations, including from our HQ and hub locations, client site or home. Travel is part of life at Opencast, and takes in account requirements of your work, our clients and your team.   We include you    We welcome candidates from all identities, attributes, ways of thinking and backgrounds to thrive in a career at Opencast. Our aim is for the diversity of our people to be reflected in the solutions we deliver, to help create a fairer society for all.       Interview    Job interviews are on Microsoft Teams. We’ll make any adjustments to help you.

jobs.description: Our mission We're making Africa the first cashless continent. In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash. We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast. Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in... How you'll help us achieve it We're looking for a CTO who wants to own engineering end to end: the systems, the people, and the standards for a company whose work changes lives. Keep us moving fast as we get bigger: We deliberately favour fewer processes, simple designs, and deeply understood tools, because that's what lets a small team operate a system this important. Your job is to protect that as the headcount grows and ensure more ownership per engineer, and a clear view of where complexity is worth the tradeoff. Own reliability: Wave is the financial system for tens of millions of people. You'll set the standards for uptime, incident response, and how carefully we change things that move money and you'll be accountable when we fall short. Build and lead the leadership layer: You'll inherit 5 direct reports and an engineering organization of ~100 people including security, data and infrastructure. You will be responsible for hiring, developing, and where necessary replacing engineering managers and directors. You'll be personally involved in senior hiring. Set our vision on AI: Set our vision on AI. We're already seeing AI accelerate product velocity, but we think we're in the early days of what we can do with AI in our apps and to move faster across the org. We want you to make Wave a truly AI forward organization. Support expansion. Wave already has over 25M users with accelerating growth. This scale and each new market brings new challenges and constraints. You'll help us plan the right architecture and organisational structure to help us grow smoothly and consistently. Represent engineering to the company. Wave is very transparent, whether that's defaulting to public conversations in slack, frequent Ask Wave Anything sessions, or defaulting to writing public docs to explain major decisions. You'll communicate openly and clearly about what engineering is doing and why, to an audience that includes engineers, non-engineers, our leadership team, and our when needed regulators. Engineering teams are co-led by Product Managers and an engineering manager.  Stack: Python 3 with mypy on the backend, GraphQL API layer, Postgres and Redis, Kotlin/Jetpack on Android (our main client), Swift/SwiftUI on iOS, TypeScript and React on the web. Infrastructure on GCP, managed with Kubernetes and Terraform. Most backend work happens in a large Python monolith, deployed across multi-country architecture. jobs.description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>Our Global Structure</strong></p> <p><br>Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.</p></div><h2>Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.</h2> <p>We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.</p> <p>This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.</p> <p>We are now looking for a <strong>Backend Engineer (Golang)</strong> to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.</p> <p>This role will be based in <strong>London</strong>, <strong>UK</strong> as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.</p> <h3>What you'll do:</h3> <ul> <li>Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.</li> <li>Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.</li> <li>Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.</li> <li>Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.</li> <li>Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.</li> <li>Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.</li> <li>Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. jobs.title: Engineering Manager - Authentication & Authorisation
jobs.description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to join our Authentication and Authorisation team where you'll be responsible for the strategy, delivery and outcomes for the Pleo’s product IAM. This is a highly complex space with a legacy custom-built service and a future-state platform, currently being implemented in our Enterprise rewrite. Success in this role means defining and executing a sensible migration path between SMB and Enterprise architectures and modernising our current auth capabilities while maintaining high security, compliance, performance and trust. Who you'll be working with and reporting to You’ll report to our VP of Engineering and you’ll lead, mentor and grow a team of 6- 10 software engineers. You’ll work closely with Product, Security, Compliance and Core Platform teams to align priorities and manage dependencies, and you’ll collaborate across the wider Backend & Infrastructure group to keep technical direction and platform standards coherent. Ultimately, your role is to foster an environment where engineers can do their best work and grow - as individuals and as a team - by setting clear expectations, ensuring our ways of working enable delivery (rather than slowing it down) and holding a high bar for quality. What you'll be doing As an Engineering Manager, you will: Own the vision, strategy and execution roadmap for identity, authentication and authorisation across SMB and Enterprise. Drive delivery and outcomes for the Authentication & Authorisation team, ensuring we build secure, scalable systems the whole platform can rely on. Successfully roll out a new identity platform across our Enterprise offerings. Define and execute a pragmatic migration strategy between the SMB legacy service and the Enterprise architecture. Update legacy auth services, reducing risk and technical debt while maintaining high security, compliance, performance and trust. Partner closely with Product, Security, Compliance and Core Platform teams to align priorities, unblock dependencies and keep delivery moving. Stay close to the technology and architecture, stepping into technical discussions to guide the team through complex trade-offs. Continuously improve how we build software - strengthening operational excellence, quality and ways of working. Hire, coach and grow a high-performing team, helping people develop while building trust and strong team dynamics. What you bring Must have Solid experience as an Engineering Manager (or equivalent people-lead role), with meaningful people leadership impact (including coaching and performance support). Strong hands-on technical depth in authentication and authorisation domains and standards (e.g. OAuth, SAML, OIDC) and modern identity platforms (e.g. Amazon Cognito, Auth0, Stytch) within a product centric organisation. Architect

jobs.title: Senior Frontend Engineer
jobs.description: About Us Plentific is a property technology platform used by housing providers, local authorities, housing associations, asset managers, and contractors across the UK and Germany to coordinate repairs, maintenance, and contractor workflows at scale. The platform combines a marketplace, workflow automation, and operational analytics, and is built to handle the volume and compliance demands of social housing, local authority property portfolios, and large-scale residential operations. We are headquartered in London and our team works across Europe. We are growing the team to expand the platform's coverage across Europe and to integrate AI throughout the product and operating model. If you are interested in working on hard, real-world problems in a sector that has long been under-served by good software, we would like to hear from you. The Role We are hiring a Senior Frontend Engineer to build the product surfaces that housing providers, contractors, and residents use every day. This is a fully remote position; we currently have remote engineers based in the UK, Germany, Turkey, Poland, Italy, Spain, and Portugal. You will report to a Team Lead, a hands-on engineer who still writes code and has a small number of engineers reporting to them, and work alongside product managers, designers, backend engineers, and data analysts. Our frontend is built on TypeScript, React, React Router, TanStack Query, MaterialUI and BaseUI, against an increasingly service-oriented backend built in Django REST Framework and PostgreSQL. The codebase is large but clean, because we put real weight on design patterns, readability, testability, maintainability, and extendability. The engineering team sits at the centre of what Plentific does, and the problems are genuinely difficult: online payments, quoting, invoicing, booking, search and scoring algorithms, in-app messaging, real-time notifications, and fraud prevention. Much of it is high-volume and messy legacy integrations, complex permissions, strict compliance requirements, and users who need software to fit how work actually happens on the ground. We expect you to apply engineering judgement to these problems rather than only writing the code in front of you, and to treat agentic, spec-driven development as a normal part of how you work rather than an experiment. Success in this role means shipping interfaces that are fast, accessible, and well-tested, raising the standard of the frontend codebase around you, and leaving the engineers you work with better than you found them. Key Responsibilities Frontend Engineering Build and maintain product interfaces in TypeScript, React, TanStack Query, React Router, MaterialUI and BaseUI across our web applications. Translate product requirements and design concepts into technical documents that set out scope, system behaviour, edge cases, and high-level technical analysis. Design component APIs, state management, and data-fetching patterns that stay readable and extendable as the codebase grows. Integrate against REST APIs in a service-oriented architecture, shaping the contracts with backend engineers rather than accepting whatever is offered. Review, refactor, and retire existing code so it meets the requirements of improved or new features. Performance, Quality, and Reliability Diagnose and resolve page load, rendering, and other frontend performance problems. Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests that give the team confidence to ship frequently. Instrument frontend observability with tools such as Sentry, Grafana Logs or New Relic, and act on what they show. Debug and fix production issues across our applications, including the integration points where frontend and backend behaviour diverge. Design against common frontend security risks, including XSS and CSRF. Agentic and Spec-Driven Development Turn ambiguous product ideas into implementation-ready specs, including user flows, component behaviour, edge cases, acceptance criteria, and test expec

jobs.title: Network Operation Engineer
jobs.description: Network Operations Engineer 1. About the role Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it. For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar. We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling. The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes. You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it. 2. What you'll do Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing. Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with. Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state. Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online. Move the work forward. You are part of the network team

jobs.title: AI Research Engineer (Kernel & Inference Optimization)
jobs.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Research Engineer (Kernel & Inference Optimization) based in France. You will work at the intersection of AI research, systems engineering, and high-performance model inference. Your focus will be on developing and optimizing model-serving architectures for advanced AI systems across a range of hardware environments. You will tackle challenges involving latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and scalability, including deployment on resource-constrained mobile and edge devices. The role combines hands-on research with low-level engineering, giving you the opportunity to develop novel inference strategies and GPU kernels. You will work with complex architectures spanning text, image, audio, diffusion models, and vision transformers. Your work will involve rigorous benchmarking, production testing, and iterative optimization to translate research into measurable performance improvements. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams in a highly technical, remote environment focused on pushing the boundaries of efficient AI systems. Accountabilities Design and deploy advanced model-serving architectures optimized for high throughput, low latency, and efficient memory utilization. Develop inference pipelines capable of operating effectively across diverse environments, including resource-constrained mobile devices and edge platforms. Establish clear performance targets covering response latency, token generation speed, throughput, memory footprint, and reliability. Build and execute controlled inference benchmarks in simulated and production environments, tracking latency, throughput, memory consumption, and error rates. Create and maintain representative datasets and simulation scenarios for evaluating model performance under real-world and resource-constrained conditions. Identify computational and memory bottlenecks across inference pipelines and implement solutions involving batching, networking, memory management, and other system-level optimizations. Develop custom GPU kernels and compute shaders for mobile hardware, including solutions written in Metal Shading Language (MSL). Apply advanced inference optimization techniques such as pruning, quantization, Flash Attention, KV caching, and speculative decoding. Design and optimize distributed inference systems using approaches such as tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and expert parallelism for large-scale GPU workloads. Work with cross-functional engineering and research teams to integrate optimized inference frameworks into production and edge-device applications. Define evaluation methodologies, document experimental results, compare performance against established benchmarks, and continuously refine optimization strategies. Monitor production performance and use empirical research to identify opportunities for further improvements in scalability, efficiency, and reliability. Requirements: Degree in Computer Science or a related technical field; a PhD in NLP, Machine Learning, or a related discipline is highly relevant, particularly with a strong AI research track record and publications at leading conferences. Proven expertise in Metal Shading Language (MSL), including the ability to write custom compute shaders from scratch. Demonstrated experience with low-level kernel optimization and inference optimization on mobile or other resource-constrained devices. Track record of delivering measurable improvements in inference latency, throughput, and memory footprint for domain-specific applications. Deep understanding of modern model-serving architectures, inference engines, and optimization techniques for high-performance AI deployment. Depuis plus de 70 ans, PRECIA MOLEN, entreprise familiale française, conçoit et fabrique des solutions de pesage de haute qualité. Nous recherchons notre prochain  Ingénieur Electronique (H/F)  sur notre agence de Bron (69) ou au siège à Veyras (07). VOTRE MISSION : Au sein du Département Recherche et Développement, votre mission sera d'imaginer et de concevoir l'électronique des produits d'aujourd'hui et de demain, en assurant leur fiabilité, leur performance et leur conformité aux exigences techniques et réglementaires. VOTRE QUOTIDIEN : Conception et développement : Rédaction de spécifications techniques et de cahiers des charges. Conception de cartes électroniques (architecture, schématique, routage) en intégrant les contraintes d'industrialisation, des processus de production, mécaniques, environnementales et normatives (CEM, sécurité électrique, Ex et ML). Programmation des drivers bas niveau et de firmwares de tests. Validation fonctionnelle et qualification des prototypes. Contribution à l'élaboration des plannings de développement. Recherche et développement : Participation à des projets d'innovation dans l'objectif de concevoir l'électronique de nouveaux produits, d'ajouter de nouvelles fonctionnalités, d'améliorer les performances, de réduire les coûts des produits existants. Traitement du signal et conception analogique du conditionnement des signaux capteurs. Veille technologique et réglementaire. Support technique : Participation à la vie du laboratoire (besoins matériels et consommables, suivi des instruments de mesure...). Support aux essais environnementaux. Garant du respect des exigences réglementaires produits. Implication active au SMQ du département R&D. Investigation technique des retours clients et terrain. Des déplacements sont à prévoir en France et à l'étranger (5-6 fois par an). VOTRE PROFIL : Première expérience professionnelle dans le secteur industriel (0 à 2 ans) Connaissances en électronique analogique et numérique Compétences en simulation, tests et diagnostics Programmation (langages C / C++). Connaissances en informatique industrielle, notamment sur les bus et interfaces : I2C, SPI, UART, RS485, etc. Maîtrise des outils de CAO électronique, tels qu’Altium Designer. Compétences en analyse de données et traitement du signal Bonne connaissance des normes de sécurité électrique et de compatibilité électromagnétique (CEM) Familiarité avec les contraintes liées aux standards ATEX / IECEx Anglais professionnel : maîtrise à l’écrit et à l’oral (niveau B2 minimum). We combine the rigour of top-tier strategy consulting with deep expertise in data, digital and analytics to help clients achieve tangible business impact.</p> <p>With 2,500+ consultants, data scientists and engineers, we work with global leaders such as Samsung, L’Oréal, Orange and Sanofi. jobs.title: Engagement Manager (Strategy & Data/AI Transformation)
jobs.description: <h2>Who is Artefact?</h2> <p>Artefact is a next-generation strategy and data consulting firm dedicated to transforming organisations through data and AI. We combine the rigour of top-tier strategy consulting with deep expertise in data, digital and analytics to help clients achieve tangible business impact.</p> <p>With 2,500+ consultants, data scientists and engineers, we work with global leaders such as Samsung, L’Oréal, Orange and Sanofi. Our Zurich office is at the heart of Artefact’s growth, advising clients on their most pressing strategic challenges — from AI strategy and governance to digital transformation roadmaps and new business model design.</p> <h2>Main Responsibilities</h2> <p>As an Engagement Manager in our Zurich or Lausanne office, you will work at the intersection of strategy consulting and data and AI delivery. You will:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Strategy Development:</strong> Work with client leadership teams to address high-stakes questions. How can AI reshape our business model? How should we govern and organise for data? Which strategic programmes deliver the most impact?</li> <li><strong>Structured Problem-Solving:</strong> Break complex challenges down into decisions a client can act on, combining consulting rigour with a working knowledge of what current AI can and cannot actually do.</li> <li><strong>Solution Design:</strong> Turn a business question into a solution shape — what data it depends on, what kind of platform or product it should sit on, and what “good” looks like once it is built. You will do this alongside our data scientists and engineers, and you will be accountable for whether the design survives contact with production.</li> <li><strong>Project Delivery:</strong> Run engagements end to end, from hypothesis framing and market and competitor analysis through to data maturity assessments, client workshops, governance design and implementation roadmaps.</li> <li><strong>Feasibility &amp; Economics:</strong> Own the answer to "will this work, and what will it cost". The evaluation approach, the unit economics per query or per case, and the point at which the business case stops closing.</li> <li><strong>Client Engagement:</strong> Work closely with C-level stakeholders and business unit leaders. You will build trusted relationships, communicate recommendations with clarity, and keep the work aligned to what the client is actually trying to decide.</li> <li><strong>Team Leadership:</strong> Lead mixed teams of consultants, data scientists and engineers. You are the person who can tell whether the technical plan is realistic, and the person the client believes when you say that it is.</li> <li><strong>Knowledge &amp; Practice Building:</strong> Contribute to the growth of Artefact's Zurich and Lausanne offices by shaping new offerings, creating intellectual capital - frameworks, thought pieces, benchmarks - and taking part in business development.</li> </ul> <h2>Candidate Profile</h2> <p>We are looking for someone who can hold a technical position and a commercial one at the same time, and lead a team through both. The strongest candidates meet most of the following.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Education:</strong> A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Business, Economics or a related field. A strong technical foundation counts for more with us than where you studied.</li> <li><strong>Work Experience:</strong> Five to eight years across consulting and technology delivery, including at least one dedicated AI or data project.</li> <li><strong>Business Acumen &amp; AI Fluency:</strong> A strong dual affinity

jobs.description: About the role Imagine owning the quality backbone of an aerospace company moving at full speed. While innovation accelerates around you, you ensure every design and every process meets the highest standards without slowing the momentum. As the Engineering Quality Manager, you will ensure that our engineering Organisation (including the Design Organization (DO)) maintains compliance with applicable standards and best practices (like EASA Part 21 Subpart J, EN9100). You’ll lead the development and oversight of our quality system, manage design supplier qualification and monitoring, drive internal and external audits and continuous improvement across all design, qualification and certification activities. At Destinus , we are revolutionizing the defense industry with cutting-edge Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our innovative technologies are designed to meet the unique demands of modern defense operations, delivering unparalleled speed, precision, and cost effectiveness. Destinus partners with government agencies and defense organizations worldwide to provide advanced solutions for mission-critical operations, enabling a new era of efficiency and technological superiority. Join us in shaping the future of defense with groundbreaking aerospace innovations. What You´ll Do Be responsible for establishing, documenting, developing and managing the Quality System and for ensuring that it continues to comply with regulatory requirements and business needs. Support and guide our Engineering departments in the definition and implementation of efficient processes. Oversee design supplier qualification, categorization, and ongoing performance monitoring. Maintain and enhance the quality system, including document control, change management, and compliance monitoring Monitor compliance of internal processes with established industry standards and certification authority requirements (such as EN9100, EASA Part 21J and required military standards). Plan, conduct, and document internal and external audits in line with established processes. Track and follow up on audit findings and corrective actions. Collaborate with stakeholders and external auditors (e.g., EASA, MoD), and cross-functional teams to ensure compliance and quality standards are met. Requirements What You’ll Need 7+ years in military or civil aviation or aerospace quality and compliance, or other highly quality driven industries such as automotive, energy with hands-on experience in the aviation industry Experience with supplier quality management. Track record in leading quality investigations, undertaking root cause analysis, developing corrective action plans, and ensuring the effectiveness of actions undertaken. Audit training/certification or experience setting up  ISO 9001, AS9100, AQAP2110 quality systems required. Familiarity with EASA Part 21 Subpart J and industry certification standards (e.g., DO-178C, DO-254, STANAGs). Strong communication, analytical, and cross-functional collaboration skills Who You Are You are naturally detail obsessed but never lose sight of the bigger picture. You combine regulatory sharpness with practical engineering judgment and you know when to challenge and when to enable. Calm under pressure, you bring structure to complexity and clarity to ambiguity. You are assertive without ego, collaborative without compromising standards. When something is not compliant, you speak up. When a process can be better, you improve it.   Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

jobs.description: <p>RDQ327R180</p> <p><strong>Staff Security Engineer, Incident Response</strong></p> <p>The Incident Response team's mission is to respond to security threats, incidents and investigations to protect our customers, employees and enterprise data in a fast, efficient and standardised manner. We're a tight-knit team of security incident responders and incident handlers doing "Security for Databricks on Databricks", using our own platform to create near-real-time log analytics, alerting and forensics.</p> <p>You will be an individual contributor on the security Incident Response (IR) team at Databricks, reporting to the regional IR manager. You will be a security multiplier and help the team scale security incident response at Databricks.</p> <p><strong>The impact you will have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You will respond to incidents as part of a distributed 24x7 operations and on-call schedule.</li> <li>You will triage and respond to security events and alerts, ensuring quick and effective containment.</li> <li>You will conduct analysis and forensics across a range of data sources to determine the timeline and impact of security events.</li> <li>You will provide technical leadership and influence team direction.</li> <li>You will develop solutions, including leveraging AI and agentic platforms, to deliver autonomous capabilities, expedite your work and scale the impact of the team.</li> <li>You will communicate technical decisions through design docs and tech talks, and mentor junior security responders via security guidance, design reviews and code reviews.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we look for:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's Degree AND 7+ years experience in Incident Response work OR Master's Degree AND 5+ years experience.</li> <li>Cloud security expertise in at least 1 of AWS, GCP or Azure, and proficiency in the others.</li> <li>Proficiency in AI/LLM and agentic capabilities. Prefer experience with building and operating agentic systems in a security setting.</li> <li>Broad security subject matter expertise.</li> <li>Expertise in a few core IR skills (DFIR , Reverse Engineering, Traditional Network Security, Storage and access security, Sandboxing, Compute security, etc.).</li> <li>Experience with Enterprise Security and SaaS applications.</li> <li>Working knowledge of a SIEM and SOAR.</li> <li>Experience building Incident Response Tooling, scripting language skills and experience with AI coding tools.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>About Databricks</strong></p> <p><span style="font-family: arial, sans-serif;">Databricks is the Data and AI company. jobs.description: <p>The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.</p> <p>Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App.&nbsp;Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p>Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Overview</strong></p> <p style="text-align: left;" data-speechify-sentence="">The Platform team owns the backend behind everything Speechify ships: the public TTS API,&nbsp;payments, subscriptions, auth, consumption tracking, and analytics — serving over 50&nbsp;million users across iOS, Android, Mac, Chrome, and web.</p> <p style="text-align: left;" data-speechify-sentence="">These are systems where correctness compounds. Subscription state has to stay consistent&nbsp;across five clients and two app-store billing systems that each go quiet at the worst moment.&nbsp;Consumption metering has to be exact enough to bill on and cheap enough to run at our&nbsp;request volume. The public TTS API has external customers with their own products&nbsp;depending on our latency and uptime. None of this degrades gracefully — it is either right, or&nbsp;someone gets charged twice.</p> <p data-speechify-sentence="">The job is to make your own job smaller. Every system you own here should need less of&nbsp;you a year from now than it did the day you took it, and the reward for that is a larger one.&nbsp;That is the entire growth path on this team — there is no separate ladder, and no ceiling&nbsp;except the one you stop raising. We are a flat organization: people become leaders here by&nbsp;taking scope and being right about it, fast.</p> <p><strong>What Yo</strong><strong>u’</strong><strong>ll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li data-speechify-sentence="">Design, build, and own the APIs behind payments, subscriptions, auth, consumption&nbsp;tracking, and our public TTS API</li> <li data-speechify-sentence="">Take on services you didn't write and make them faster, cheaper, and harder to break</li> <li data-speechify-sentence="">Establish that a change is correct before it ships, and leave behind the checks that keep it&nbsp;correct after you've moved on</li> <li data-speechify-sentence="">Automate the parts of your role that shouldn't need a person, then go take on what that&nbsp;freed you up for</li> <li data-speechify-sentence="">Turn work you've done once into work the whole team can repeat</li> <li data-speechify-sentence="">Design B2B and enterprise integrations for customers building on top of us</li> <li data-speechify-sentence="">Work with product, mobile, and web to keep backend architecture ahead of where the&nbsp;product is going</li> </ul> <p><strong>An Ideal Candidate Should Have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Proven backend experience in TS/Node (required)</li> <li>Direct experience with GCP; working knowledge of AWS, Azure, or another cloud</li> <li>A habit of giving away work you used to own, and something to show for the room it&nbsp;created</li> <li>A daily working setup with AI agents you can describe in detail

jobs.title: Product Engineer
jobs.description: The Context Banks still run their most critical, regulated work by hand; reading letters and emails, re-keying data between systems, chasing down missing info. It's the kind of work that's too important to get wrong and too tedious for anyone to want to do. Porters fixes this. Our AI agents run these regulated processes end to end, with the audit trails and security banks actually require, so the work moves at the speed customers expect instead of the speed a backlog allows. We're just over a year old and already live with real customers, growing the product quickly, and were named Fintech of the Year 2026. The goal is to build the operating system for autonomous banking. We're backed by Earlybird, one of Europe's oldest venture firms, and Seedcamp, who wrote first checks into Revolut, Wise, and UiPath. The Mission You'll own features in their entirety. Self-standing or with guidance of founders and fellow engineers, you turn a clear problem statement into a strong design and build, test, and ship new features that directly enable our customers. You integrate features across our layered stack, from the API to the data plane, and carry them all the way to production. This job is in person in Zurich, or remote in Barcelona or Berlin. Your responsibilities Ship features end-to-end: Deliver complete vertical slices across the stack, from the API layer to the data model, carried through to running in production. Grow what the platform does for banks: Build the services Porters performs for banks: Extend the capabilities of our agentic platform such as case handling, customer matching, AI tool integrations, data enrichment, or keeping humans in the loop. Deliver features that hold together as a system: Design endpoints, contracts, and interfaces that work together, ensuring features integrate cleanly towards one bigger outcome. Ensure your work is reliable: Own design, development, tests, and deployment, so what reaches production is proven to work. Wow our customers: You solve for the customer's actual problem, not just the request and measure success by customer outcomes. What would it take for the customer to say “Porters, made my day”. Your profile Experience: Around 4 years of professional software engineering, with a track record of shipping in fast-paced, ambiguous environments. Regulated industry and/or VC-backed startup experiences are a plus. Product thinking: You naturally understand why you’re building something, not just focusing on how to build. Quality focus & individual problem solving: Given a clear problem, you reliably produce a clean algorithm, a sensible data model, a well-structured service. You treat tests and observability as part of the feature, and right-size rigor to risk. You are comfortable in a regulated fintech environment where precision matters. Technical proficiency: Proficiency in Python is mandatory, along with REST API development, an ORM, and relational databases. AI-native: You've worked with, or are eager to work with, LLM/agentic tooling, and understand how to bound probabilistic output with deterministic code. Collaboration and eagerness to learn: You thrive on direction, review, and challenge, take feedback well, and want to grow into larger scopes. You are eager to learn every day. Going the extra mile: Be part of a high-growth phase, where we move fast and expect focused intensity. 9-to-5 is not the mode we work in, if you want to build something that matters with a team that ships, we are your people. What We Offer Ownership from day one: Real features running in production at major financial institutions, with the trust to carry them there yourself. Founder collaboration: Work directly with founders who have built and scaled fintech and analytics products before. We win and lose together as a team: We expect people to leave their comfort zone on a daily basis, however, we work together as a team and support each other at any time. Growth: A dedicated development budget, free to use

jobs.title: Founding Engineer (Tech Lead)
jobs.description: The Context Banks still run their most critical, regulated work by hand; reading letters and emails, re-keying data between systems, chasing down missing info. It's the kind of work that's too important to get wrong and too tedious for anyone to want to do. Porters fixes this. Our AI agents run these regulated processes end to end, with the audit trails and security banks actually require, so the work moves at the speed customers expect instead of the speed a backlog allows. We're just over a year old and already live with real customers, growing the product quickly, and were named Fintech of the Year 2026. The goal is to build the operating system for autonomous banking. We're backed by Earlybird, one of Europe's oldest venture firms, and Seedcamp, who wrote first checks into Revolut, Wise, and UiPath. The Mission You'll own the outcomes. You take an ambiguous business problem and turn it into clear requirements, a design with clear business rationale, sequenced work, and a realistic estimate, build the hardest parts yourself, and multiply a team of mid-level engineers with well-defined, extensible work and the reviews that keep quality high. You stay an IC at heart while making the work legible, sized, and worth doing. This job is in person in Zurich, or remote in Barcelona or Berlin. Your responsibilities Deliver the highest-risk work yourself: Be the IC where it matters. Personally engineer the most complex, business-critical components, from cross-service logic to the boundary where AI outputs become deterministic, auditable actions, and set the technical bar for the team as you go. Turn business goals into shipped projects: Take an ambiguous problem and own it through to delivery, defining requirements, a design that starts from customer impact and takes the highest-ROI path whether it's make or buy, sequenced work, estimates, and clear engineering acceptance criteria a team can execute with minimal churn. Design complex systems that don’t break down in 12 months: Architect entire systems so the likely next requirement plugs in cleanly through configuration or a new adapter, keeping components reusable and loosely coupled, separating business logic from shared services, and maintaining a single authoritative, append-only source of truth for critical data - including consideration of make-or-buy options. Scale the team's autonomy and quality: Set decision thresholds so engineers self-serve low-stakes calls, define sanctioned paths for experimenting with regulated data, and spread understanding of our systems to cut key-person risk. Settle design in review, then build the road to production: CI/CD with quality gates, automated migrations, and systems that report their own health. Wow our customers: You solve for the customer's actual problem, not just the request, and measure success by customer outcomes. What would it take for the customer to say “Porters made my day!”? Your profile Experience: Typically 8+ years of professional software engineering, with a track record of shipping in fast-paced, ambiguous environments. You will sit inside the product delivery team that focuses on user growth, working closely with the person accountable for that part of the business and with the engineers building it. And you will not be doing it alone: You join a group of Conversion Design Analysts across the company who work the same way and hold each other's standards. English is our working language. Frame the real problem before solving it. Dig into quantitative and qualitative data until you find the actual question underneath the ask. Then make it explainable and actionable. A well-framed problem is half the battle Design, run the experiment, read it honestly and decide what comes next. Define a testable change, get it instrumented properly, and analyse the outcome. Then use what you learned to frame the next question. That includes reporting the tests that did not work, and designing the next step. Talk to neighbours. Experiments tell you what happened, not what people needed. You will spend real time with the people who use this, because you cannot A/B test your way to understanding somebody. Direct AI, and spend your judgment where it counts. AI produces a lot of our first-pass design. You will brief it, push back on it, and hold the quality bar, so your own hours go to the thinking a model cannot do. Argue for cutting things. Adding is easy. You have statistical literacy. You don’t need to be able to run R, but you understand what Bayesian vs. frequentist is about and why you do a power analysis before launching an experiment. You care about craft and are attentive to details. You can tell the difference between good enough and actually good and you design experiences people do not have to think about. You present your work clearly, defend your decisions when challenged, and are comfortable in front of a crowd. You are fluent with AI tools. jobs.title: Cyber Security Engineer — Infrastructure & AI Platform Security (w/m/d)
jobs.description: Über IONOS Bei IONOS verwalten wir nicht nur Server, wir prägen mit unseren Lösungen die digitale Zukunft für über 6,2 Millionen Kundinnen und Kunden weltweit. Als Europas führender Hosting-Anbieter und Pionier für unabhängige Cloud-Lösungen bauen wir eine Infrastruktur der nächsten Generation: von souveränen Cloud-Architekturen und hochperformanten GPU-Clustern bis hin zu integrierten KI-Automatisierungstools. Was uns antreibt: Digitale Entscheidungsfreiheit für Europa und echter Impact für kleine und mittlere Unternehmen (KMU) sowie Großunternehmen. Wir arbeiten in agilen Teams, setzen auf transparente Strukturen und glauben daran, dass Exzellenz und Innovation nur mit echtem Teamgeist entstehen. Bereit für Deinen nächsten Schritt? Werde ein Teil von IONOS und wachse mit uns. Beide Hälften dieser Rolle drehen sich um dieselbe grundlegende Frage: Welche Systeme können unsere empfindlichste Infrastruktur erreichen und unter welchen Kontrollen. Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Sicherheitsarchitektur unserer providerseitigen Infrastrukturschicht und bist Fachexperte (m/w/d) für die intern betriebenen KI-Plattformen und -Agenten. Dabei stellst Du sicher, dass diese in einem sicheren, verwalteten und auditierbaren Zustand laufen, anstatt sich schleichend als neue Klasse von privilegierten Zugriffen anzuhäufen. Dies ist eine praxisnahe Expertenrolle. Du setzt Standards, prüfst Designs auf Herz und Nieren und arbeitest direkt mit Plattform- und Engineering-Teams über all unsere Marken hinweg zusammen, um diese umzusetzen. Aufgabenbereich Infrastruktursicherheit Definieren und Pflegen von Sicherheitsarchitektur-Standards und Härtungs-Baselines für providerseitige Infrastruktur: Virtualisierungs- und Container-Plattformen, Control Planes und Bereitstellungssysteme, DNS, Mail-Infrastruktur sowie Backup- und Wiederherstellungssysteme. Bewerten und Stärken der Mandantenisolierung über Shared-Hosting-, Virtualisierungs- und Container-Schichten hinweg sowie Treiben von Behebungsmaßnahmen mit den verantwortlichen Plattform-Teams. Überprüfen von Infrastruktur-Designs und wesentlichen Änderungen auf Sicherheitsauswirkungen sowie Agieren als Eskalationsinstanz für Fragen zur Infrastruktursicherheit aus Plattform-, Cloud- und Marken-Engineering-Teams. Reduzieren des Blast Radius auf den wichtigsten Pfaden: privilegierter Zugriff auf kundenorientierte Infrastruktur, administrative Segmentierung, Umgang mit Secrets und Wiederherstellungsintegrität — übersetzt in umsetzbare markenspezifische Implementierungspläne für unsere heterogenen Plattformen. Unterstützen von Cyber Defense, Vulnerability Management und IT-Notfallmanagement mit Infrastruktur-Expertise bei Vorfällen und der Nachbereitung/Härtung. Interne KI-Plattform- und Agentensicherheit Verantwortung für die Sicherheitsarchitektur und Baseline-Standards für die intern betriebenen KI-Plattformen: Modell-Gateways und self-hosted Modelle, Agenten-Frameworks, Assistenten-Integrationen, Konnektoren und Retrieval-Pipelines über interne Daten. Definieren und Durchsetzen, wie Agenten identifiziert, authentifiziert und autorisiert werden: Umgang mit nicht-menschlichen Identitäten, Credential- und Token-Management, Least-Privilege-Zugriff auf Tools und Systeme sowie Festlegung, wo autonomes Handeln ein Human-in-the-Loop erfordert. Festlegen, welche Daten interne KI-Systeme aufrufen und indexieren dürfen, sowie Sicherstellen, dass Agentenaktivitäten protokolliert, zuordenbar und überprüfbar sind — entsprechend den Anforderungen unserer regulatorischen Verpflichtungen und Zertifizierungen. Durchführen von Pre-Deployment-Sicherheitsprüfungen für neue interne KI-Plattformen und Agenten-Anwendungsfälle im Einklang mit dem schnellen Tempo der Adaption sowie Überblicken von ungesicherter/unsanktionierter KI-Nutzung (Shadow AI). Beraten der Sicherheitsfunktionen und internen Engineering-Teams bei der sicheren Einführung von KI, einschließlich der Schutzplanken (Guardrails), die eine vertretbare Einfüh
